paper_metadata.title: Multiobjective variational quantum optimization for constrained problems: an application to Cash Management

summary: The paper proposes MOVCO, a multiobjective variational method for the Cash Management Problem, and benchmarks it on classically simulated VQE circuits with 8192 shots. On 120 random CMP instances with 2 cash points over 2, 3, and 4 days, the method reaches full constraint satisfaction after about 200 generations, and in the 4-day comparison it outperforms penalty-based VQE; larger product-state experiments extend to 10-22 cash points and up to 308 variables, again showing MOVCO better than the penalty baseline.

experiments.description: MOVCO-VQE applied to randomly generated Cash Management Problem (CMP) instances, using a one-layer hardware-efficient VQE ansatz and NSGA-II multiobjective classical optimization; evaluated on problem sizes with 2 cash points over 2, 3, and 4 days.

algorithm.variant: MOVCO-VQE (Multi-Objective Variational Constrained Optimizer with VQE)
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Ry rotations and nearest-neighbor CZ entangling gates
algorithm.optimizer: NSGA-II (binary tournament selection, simulated binary crossover, polynomial mutation)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed number of generations / evaluations; results reported up to 400 generations and 8192 shots per evaluation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameters initialized around pi/4 with small random perturbations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary/spin variables encode discretized cash levels; total qubits/variables V = 2CD for the main experiments
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize transaction cost C(z) subject to cash-balance and network constraints; MOVCO optimizes two objectives: constraint satisfaction percentage P(theta) and restricted energy E(theta) over feasible states
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: feasibility filter / multiobjective optimization (maximize constraint satisfaction and minimize restricted energy); no penalty terms in MOVCO
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: C(z) given in Eq. (16) of the paper; a diagonal Hamiltonian in Pauli-Z operators encoding transaction costs

problem_instance.description: Cash Management Problem for ATM/branch cash delivery scheduling

dataset_specification.description: cash-point counts C=2; periods D=2,3,4 days; prices kc drawn from discrete uniform [1,4] with first-day price doubled; initial predictions Pcd drawn from discrete uniform [-2,5]; last-day total cash limit v=C; daily transaction limit l=1 if C=2 otherwise floor(C/2)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: discretization of cash levels with h=4 allowed values; normalized cash variable Mct = 3/2 + (1/2) z_ct with z_ct in {-1,+1}
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: classical simulation of the quantum circuit; 120 instances; 8192 shots; metrics averaged over instances with confidence/percentile intervals; up to 400 generations

hardware.framework: pymoo for classical optimization; quantum circuit classically simulated (framework not explicitly named)

noise_model.noise_type: noise-free classical simulation of quantum circuit

implementation_details.classical_solver: NSGA-II (for MOVCO-VQE); SPSA used only in the penalty-VQE comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: random instance generation; discretization of cash levels; mapping to spin variables
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Pareto-front ranking; approximation ratio and success-rate analysis

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: two-stage behavior: first constraint satisfaction increases, then restricted energy decreases

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum speedup claim is made; results are from classical simulation of a gate-based variational circuit.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not established; no hardware crossover analysis
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a real QPU implementation of the variational circuit and a classical baseline comparison at matched wall-clock cost
limiting_factors: Classical genetic optimizer (NSGA-II) is part of the method
Performance is compared only against a penalty-based VQE, not against strong classical CMP solvers

notes: Hardware is a classical simulation of the VQE circuit; no real QPU is used.
Num qubits inferred from the paper's explicit formula V = 2CD and the benchmark settings C=2 with D=2,3,4; 16 qubits explicitly stated for the 4-day comparison.
Speedup order is not analyzed in the paper; set to none_proven.
